scope: Generic WIC air-cooled condenser/high-side and compressor behavior; model-specific operating envelope remains equipment data.
principles: High condensing pressure is a system condition, not a diagnosis.
Condenser airflow/heat-rejection faults, charge/noncondensables, head-pressure controls and ambient/load must be discriminated before naming a root cause.
Low condensing pressure can be caused by low load/low suction, compressor valve leakage/capacity loss, excessive effective condenser capacity, or head-pressure-control issues.
Low-ambient head-pressure controls intentionally alter condenser/receiver behavior; interpret pressures and refrigerant inventory with that configuration known.
A hot compressor is an effect with several possible system causes; do not condemn the compressor from temperature alone.
Compressor capacity/pumping diagnosis requires system pressures plus operating/electrical/model context; model operating-envelope limits are not generic.

domains.condition: Condensing pressure/temperature is above the applicable operating expectation.
discriminators: condenser entering ambient and leaving air
domains.diagnosis_policy: Require localized heat-rejection/control/charge evidence; high head alone does not identify dirty coil or overcharge.

domains.condition: Condensing pressure is below the applicable system/control expectation.
causes: head-pressure regulator set too low or malfunctioning
compressor suction/discharge valve leakage or capacity loss
domains.diagnosis_policy: Low head in low ambient may be a control/configuration problem, not refrigerant charge.

domains.condition: Air-cooled condenser cannot reject heat normally because airflow is inadequate or recirculated.
supporting: hot discharge air recirculates to inlet
domains.diagnosis_policy: Use local visual/airflow/fan evidence before localizing.

domains.condition: Low-ambient/head-pressure control does not maintain intended condensing/receiver pressure.
causes: insufficient flood charge for control design
domains.diagnosis_policy: Only apply when such controls are actually installed; do not treat their deliberate condenser flooding as ordinary overcharge.

domains.condition: Compressor/discharge temperature is excessive for the applicable model/application.
causes: high compression ratio from high head and/or very low suction
high evaporator load/high suction causing overload
domains.diagnosis_policy: Temperature alone is not proof of compressor mechanical failure.

domains.condition: Running compressor does not create expected pressure differential/capacity.
causes: internal suction/discharge valve leakage or mechanical wear
discriminators: response to load/pump-down where manufacturer permits
domains.diagnosis_policy: Do not use a universal pump-down pressure or compression-ratio limit; use compressor model/application/refrigerant data.
